notes: Accept, with two corrections made in place. The recorded hash of arXiv 1310.7692v2 reproduces (8833a226…) and I re-extracted all 42 pages. Structure: 56 items, every one of the 50 missing items routed exactly once, no routed item that is planned or library, all eight stage ids present in data/atlas.json, all five planned layer ids present, and check_paper.py passes. Coverage is complete in a checkable sense: the paper declares 49 numbered environments (Theorems 1–44, A.1–A.8, Propositions, Lemmas, Corollaries, Definitions and Remark 4) and every one of them appears in an item. Locators: of 66 name-and-page checks, 65 land on exactly the page given, and the one that does not is right too — item 13 cites p.34 for the Dembo–Poonen–Shao–Zeitouni input inside the proof of Theorem 7, which begins on p.33 and reaches that citation on p.34. Correction 1: item 21 (the Kummer identification H¹(K, μ_2) = K^×/K^{×2}) was marked library, but neither library has it. TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective gives only the injection — its own docstring says surjectivity 'is what would upgrade it to the Kummer isomorphism' — and Mathlib's cited lemma is the finite-Galois Hilbert 90, not the profinite statement the surjectivity needs; a name search for Kummer, H1 and Hilbert 90 declarations over both pinned trees found nothing stronger. The paper prints the identification as an equality on p.8, so the item now has status planned at the Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology roadmap's Layer 9, which plans Hilbert 90 for G_K and then the Kummer sequence and isomorphism; the two declarations and the corrected name TauCeti.kummerClassMap_injective (the file path, not the namespace, carries FieldTheory) are kept in the note. Correction 2: E1's correction text gave the sign of the failing pairing in the Weierstrass case as +1; my computation and E1's own reason give −1 for g ≥ 2, and that clause is corrected. All five findings are confirmed, each recomputed or re-read rather than taken on trust: E1's Gram matrices were recomputed symbolically for g = 1, 2, 3 in both cases, printed and corrected planes; E2's two elliptic curves have discriminants 2⁵·5·7·79·7919 and −571, and the corrected curve is isomorphic over Q to y² = x³ − 27Ix − 27J with u = 6; E3's missing hypothesis at 2 is exactly the case where one of p, q is ≡ 3 mod 4 and the other ≡ 5 mod 8, and no prime other than p, q and 2 can have a unique prime above it in Q(√p, √q); E4's proof on p.26 states the hypothesis as 16Z and Theorem 15 claims κ = 4; E5's four slips are printed as quoted, and Crossref confirms Stoll's paper as Algebra & Number Theory 1 (2007), 349–391 and Skorobogatov's monograph as 2001. I did not read the JAMS text, which returned 403, so like the extraction every verdict is about arXiv v2, and Crossref still records no correction for 10.1090/jams/863.
